mainTopic: A ברייתא about a woman who returned no longer pregnant with an unknown birth: when she may be with her husband, how many immersions she needs, and a challenge to רבי יהושע בן לוי
overview: This amud discusses a ברייתא about a woman who left home pregnant and came back no longer pregnant. We don't know when she gave birth, or whether she had a boy, a girl, or gave birth while she was a זבה. After she returned she had three clean weeks, then ten weeks switching between a week of bleeding and a clean week. The ברייתא rules that she may be with her husband only on the eve of day 35. בית שמאי require 95 immersions, בית הלל require 35, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says one immersion at the end is enough. The גמרא first uses the fourth week to challenge רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that we follow the majority. It answers for רבין that the birth may have happened long before she came back. Next, the גמרא explains why she waits until day 35: day 28 may be the first day of נדה. It also explains why day 21 and the night after it are still forbidden, using רבי שמעון's view and a case where her bleeding began at night. Finally, it starts counting בית שמאי's 95 immersions week by week, and this count continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case: a woman returns no longer pregnant
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא describes a woman who left pregnant and returned no longer pregnant. She then had three clean weeks, followed by ten weeks that switched between bleeding and clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman left home pregnant and came back no longer pregnant. In front of us she then had three clean weeks, and after that ten weeks that switched: one week impure, one week pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that sets up an unusual case of doubt about a birth. This line only describes the facts; the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key problem is that we don't know when she gave birth or what she gave birth to (boy, girl, or while she was a זבה). Each of those possibilities carries a different length of impurity. That is why the timeline of clean and bleeding weeks matters so much.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'full': pregnant
Literally 'empty': no longer pregnant
A clean week, with no bleeding
Impure; here, a week in which she saw blood

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume she gave birth right when she came back. The whole case is built on the fact that we don't know when or what she gave birth to.

phrases.english: A woman who went out full
phrases.notes: 'Full' means pregnant.

phrases.english: and came back empty,
and she brought before us three pure weeks,
phrases.notes: Meaning she spent three weeks in front of us without seeing any blood.

phrases.english: and ten weeks
one impure and one pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא that will be used against רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a birth with unknown timing and unknown type, followed by 3 clean weeks and then 10 weeks switching between bleeding and clean

steps.title: When she may be with her husband, and the dispute over the number of immersions
steps.stepSummary: She may be with her husband on the eve of the 35th day. בית שמאי require 95 immersions, and בית הלל require 35.
steps.simpleTranslation: She may be with her husband on the eve of the thirty-fifth day, and we have her immerse ninety-five times. This is the view of בית שמאי. בית הלל say: thirty-five.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its ruling: the one time she is permitted to her husband, and how many immersions she needs according to בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because we do not know when or what she gave birth to, the ברייתא is strict and waits until every doubt has passed before permitting her. The גמרא later explains the exact reason for the 35th day (step 10). The two numbers of immersions come from how many times each side requires her to immerse to cover all the possibilities, and the גמרא explains them later as well.

keyTerms.meaning: She may be with her husband
On the eve of (the night leading into) a day
We have her immerse
Immersion in a מקוה

phrases.english: She may be with her husband on the eve of the thirty-fifth,
phrases.notes: Day 35 is counted from when she came back to us.

phrases.english: and we have her immerse
ninety-five immersions,
the words of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel say: thirty-five.
phrases.notes: Thirty-five immersions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case described in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She is permitted on the eve of day 35. Immersions: 95 according to בית שמאי, 35 according to בית הלל

steps.title: A third view: one immersion at the end is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that a single immersion at the end is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: it is enough for the immersion to be at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a third opinion: she does not need to immerse again and again; one immersion at the end works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי and בית הלל both require many immersions to cover every possible moment she might need one. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that a final immersion takes care of everything before it, so only one is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for her
At the end

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא has three opinions about immersions (95, 35, or one at the end), but everyone agrees she is permitted only on the eve of day 35.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
It is enough for the immersion to be at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: דַּיָּהּ לַטְּבִילָה שֶׁתְּהֵא בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the dispute over immersions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One immersion at the end is enough

steps.title: Why the first two weeks are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining the ברייתא. Week one is forbidden because she may have had a boy, and week two because she may have had a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, in the first week she may not be with her husband: say she gave birth to a boy. In the second week, say she gave birth to a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts going through the ברייתא week by week. It is setting up a challenge (בשלמא means 'granted, this part makes sense...'), and the difficulty will come later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though she saw no blood in the first three weeks, she is still forbidden. After a boy she is impure for 7 days, which covers week one. After a girl she is impure for 14 days, which covers week two as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this part is understandable (usually leads into a difficulty)
Say / we can suppose
A woman who gave birth to a boy (7 days of impurity)
A woman who gave birth to a girl (14 days of impurity)

steps.confusionAlert: The word בשלמא does not mean the גמרא agrees with everything. It is saying 'this part works fine' before asking about a part that doesn't.

phrases.english: Granted, the first week she may not be with her husband,
say: she is a woman who gave birth to a boy;
the second week,
say: she is a woman who gave birth to a girl;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins analyzing the ברייתא in order to build a challenge against רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Week one is covered by the possibility of a boy, and week two by the possibility of a girl

steps.title: Why the third week is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Week three is forbidden because she may have given birth to a girl while she was a זבה, which requires seven clean days after the 14 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The third week: say she gave birth to a girl while she was a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues going week by week and explains the third week. It is still building toward its question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she was a זבה when she gave birth, she must count seven clean days after the 14 days of a girl. That stretches her forbidden time to three weeks. The setup is now in place for the גמרא to look at the later weeks.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who gave birth while in the status of a זבה
A woman who saw blood outside her regular time for three days, and must count seven clean days

phrases.english: the third week,
say: she is a woman who gave birth to a girl while a zava;
phrases.notes: A זבה must count seven clean days, which pushes her impurity into the third week.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁבוּעַ שְׁלִישִׁי, אֵימַר: יוֹלֶדֶת נְקֵבָה בְּזוֹב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the week-by-week explanation from step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Week three is covered by the possibility of a girl born while she was a זבה

steps.title: Why is the fourth week forbidden if it should be pure blood?
steps.stepSummary: The fourth week should be דם טוהר after a birth. Forbidding it suggests we worry she miscarried something that was not a real baby, which means we do not follow the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the fourth week, even though she sees blood, she should be allowed with her husband, because it is pure blood. Isn't the reason it is forbidden that we do not follow the majority?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from the fourth week. By then any real birth would put her in her days of pure blood, so why forbid her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the strictest case, a girl born while she was a זבה, ends the impure days after day 21. So days 22-28 should be pure blood if she gave birth to a real baby. Forbidding them only makes sense if we worry she miscarried something that is not a real birth, even though most pregnancies end in a real baby. That is not following the רוב, against רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure blood: blood seen during the set days after birth that does not make her impure
She may be with her husband
We follow the majority
Is it not because...? (a pointed question that builds a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: The worry here is not that she did not give birth. The worry is that what came out was not a full baby, so her blood would be plain נדה blood and not pure blood.

phrases.english: But the fourth week,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא חָזְיָא דָּם
phrases.english: even though she sees blood,
let her be with her husband, for it is pure blood.
phrases.notes: By day 22 even the longest impure stretch (21 days, from step 5) is over.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר רוּבָּא?
phrases.english: Is it not because we do not follow the majority?
phrases.notes: Most pregnant women give birth to a real baby. Ignoring that is "not following the majority."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר רוּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining weeks one to three, the גמרא sees that week four does not fit and uses it to challenge following the majority.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's view that we follow the majority (most births are real babies)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Week four forbidden only makes sense if we suspect a non-baby miscarriage. That means the ברייתא ignores the majority.

steps.title: So what did רבין mean by saying he saw no objection?
steps.stepSummary: Since the challenge looks strong, the גמרא asks how רבין could say he did not know what the objection was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what did he mean by 'I do not know what the objection is'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks what answer רבין had in mind when he said this ברייתא is no objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, רבין defended רבי יהושע בן לוי and said he saw no objection. Now that the fourth week seems to be a real problem, the גמרא asks what his answer would be. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what...? (asks what the real explanation is)
I do not know
A strong objection that seems to disprove a view

phrases.english: Rather, what is meant by
"I do not know what the objection is"?
phrases.notes: These are רבין's words from earlier on the daf, defending רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי לָא יָדַעְנָא מַאי תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבין would answer the challenge of step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What answer רבין had in mind for the fourth-week problem

steps.title: Maybe she gave birth long before she came back
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the birth was a real baby, but it happened long before she returned, so her pure-blood days were already over by the fourth week.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: her birth was far back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבין. The fourth week is forbidden not because of a non-baby, but because the birth may have happened long ago.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We can still follow the majority and assume a real baby. But we do not know when she gave birth. If it was long before she came back, her days of pure blood may have ended, so the blood in week four could be נדה blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / one can suggest (offers a possibility)
Her birth was far back in time

steps.whatToRemember: The fourth week does not disprove following the majority. It is forbidden because the birth may have been long ago, so her pure days may be over.

phrases.english: Say: her birth was far back.
phrases.notes: She may have given birth well before she came back, so her pure-blood days already ran out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 and so defends רבי יהושע בן לוי against step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: a different reason for being strict
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Week four is forbidden because we worry about a non-baby, so we ignore the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: We assume a real baby, but the birth may have been long ago, so the pure-blood days may be over.

steps.title: Why wait until the end of the clean fifth week?
steps.stepSummary: The fifth week had no bleeding, so why must she wait until the night of the 35th day?
steps.simpleTranslation: This fifth week, which is clean, let her be with her husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question on the ברייתא. If the fifth week is clean, why is she only allowed at its very end?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא (step 2) allows her only on the eve of the 35th day. The fifth week has no blood at all, so it seems she should be allowed earlier in that week.

keyTerms.meaning: This (Aramaic)
The fifth week

phrases.english: This fifth week,
which is clean, let her be with her husband!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָךְ שְׁבוּעַ חֲמִישִׁי דְּטָהוֹר הוּא תְּשַׁמֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from week four to week five of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that she is allowed only on the eve of the 35th day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A week with no blood should let her be allowed during it, not only at its end.

steps.title: Day 28 may be the first day of נדה
steps.stepSummary: Each bleeding day of week four may be the start of נדה. Even day 28 may be, so she needs seven days, ending on day 34.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that fourth week, every single day we are unsure whether it is the end of her birth days and the start of נדה. Even day 28 itself may be the start of נדה, so she must keep seven days for her נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the fifth week is not really free. The seven days of נדה from week four's last day still run into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we do not know when she gave birth, any day she bled in week four might be the first day after her pure days, which makes it the first day of נדה. The latest possible start is day 28, and seven days from then end on day 34. So she may only be with her husband on the night of the 35th.

keyTerms.meaning: We are in doubt
The end of her birth period (her pure-blood days)
The start of her נדה period
The seven days a נדה must keep

steps.whatToRemember: The night of day 35 comes from the strictest guess: day 28 is the first day of נדה, so seven days end on day 34.

phrases.english: That fourth week,
every single day we are in doubt
whether it is the end of the birth days and the start of נדה,
and the twenty-eighth day itself,
say it is the start of נדה,
and she must keep seven days for her נדה.
phrases.notes: Counting from day 28, the seven days end on day 34. That is why she waits until the night of the 35th.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָךְ שָׁבוּעַ רְבִיעִי כֹּל יוֹמָא וְיוֹמָא מַסְפְּקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 using the doubt about when she gave birth, from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the doubt carries into the next period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fifth week is clean, so she should be allowed during it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Day 28 may start נדה, so the seven days run through day 34 and she is allowed only on the night of the 35th.

steps.title: Why not permit her on day 21?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if week three is forbidden only because she may be a זבה counting seven clean days, she should be allowed on the 21st day.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the twenty-first day she should be allowed to be with her husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule that the whole third week is forbidden. It points out that day 21 should be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Week three is forbidden because she may have given birth as a זבה, finished the birth-impurity days, and then needed seven clean days. A זבה may immerse on the seventh clean day itself, during the day, and then be permitted. Day 21 is that seventh day, so why forbid it?

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-one, here the 21st day after she arrived

phrases.english: On the twenty-first [day] let her have relations!
phrases.notes: Day 21 would be the seventh clean day of a זבה, when she may immerse during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining week five, the גמרא goes back to challenge the ban on the end of week three.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that she may not be with her husband during the entire third week
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זבה may immerse and be permitted on her seventh clean day, which here is day 21.

steps.title: This follows רבי שמעון, who forbids the seventh day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who forbids relations on the seventh clean day in case she sees blood later that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי שמעון, who said it is forbidden to do this, because she may come into a doubtful situation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. He does not allow a זבה to be with her husband on her seventh day, even after she immerses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is with her husband on the seventh day and then sees blood later that same day, her seven clean days are cancelled. It would turn out that she was with her husband while impure. So רבי שמעון forbids it, and day 21 stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is forbidden to do so, meaning to have relations on the seventh day
A doubt or uncertain situation

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the ברייתא is following a stricter opinion about the seventh clean day of a זבה.

phrases.english: It is [the view of] רבי שמעון,
who said: "It is forbidden to do so,"
phrases.notes: "So" means being with her husband on the seventh clean day after she immerses.

phrases.english: lest she come to a doubt.
phrases.notes: If she sees blood later that day, her clean days are undone, and she may have been with her husband while impure.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed a זבה is permitted on her seventh day after immersing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who forbids the seventh day itself.

steps.title: Then permit her that night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even according to רבי שמעון, she should be permitted on the night after day 21.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let her be with her husband that evening!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. Even if day 21 is forbidden, once that day is over her seven clean days are done, so the night should be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון only worries about the seventh day itself. After night falls the count is complete with no bleeding, so his concern no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: In the evening, that night

phrases.english: Let her have relations in the evening?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of רבי שמעון by moving to the night after day 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that she is not permitted until the eve of day 35, even granting רבי שמעון's ban on day 21 itself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's worry ends once the seventh day ends, so the following night should be permitted.

steps.title: Her bleeding started in the evening
steps.stepSummary: The case is where she saw blood in the evening, so that night already belongs to the fourth week of bleeding.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about when she saw blood in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is where her bleeding started at night. So the night after day 21 is already a bleeding night of the fourth week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fourth week is a week of bleeding. If that week began in the evening, the very night we wanted to permit is a night of bleeding, so of course she is forbidden then.

keyTerms.meaning: When she saw blood
In the evening, at night

steps.whatToRemember: Day 21 is forbidden because of רבי שמעון, and the night after it is forbidden because her fourth week of bleeding started that night.

phrases.english: When she saw [blood] in the evening.
phrases.notes: Her fourth week of bleeding began at night, so that night is already a bleeding night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the night by defining the case more narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the night after day 21 was a clean night.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her fourth-week bleeding started that evening, so the night is already forbidden.

steps.title: Quoting בית שמאי: 95 immersions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the ברייתא that she must immerse 95 times, to explain how that number is reached.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we make her immerse ninety-five immersions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new section and quotes the ruling of בית שמאי that she needs 95 immersions. This is a setup line; the next steps explain the count week by week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she does not know when she gave birth or whether it was a boy or a girl, any night or day could be the moment her impurity ends. So she must immerse at every possible ending time, which adds up to 95.

keyTerms.meaning: We make her immerse in a מקוה
Immersions
Ninety-five

phrases.english: And we make her immerse
ninety-five immersions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of relations and turns to the immersion count of בית שמאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, she must immerse 95 times.

steps.title: Week one: immerse every night
steps.stepSummary: In the first week she immerses every night, in case she gave birth to a boy and her seven days ended that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the first week we make her immerse at night, since perhaps she gave birth to a boy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first part of the count. Every night of week one needs an immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who gives birth to a boy is impure for seven days. Since we do not know which day she gave birth, her seven days could end on any night of the first week. So she immerses every night, which is seven immersions.

keyTerms.meaning: The first week
At night, in the nights

phrases.english: The first week
we make her immerse at night,
phrases.notes: This means every night of that week.

phrases.english: say she gave birth to a boy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the 95 immersions quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Week one requires an immersion every night because she may have had a boy.

steps.title: Week two: immerse every night and every day
steps.stepSummary: In week two she immerses every night in case she had a girl, and every day in case she had a boy while a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the second week we make her immerse at night, since perhaps she gave birth to a girl. And by day, since perhaps she gave birth to a boy while she was a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains week two, where there are two reasons to immerse, so she immerses both at night and during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl brings fourteen days of impurity, which could end on any night of week two. If she had a boy while a זבה, after seven days of birth-impurity she counts seven clean days, and a זבה immerses during the day at the end of her count, which could be any day of week two.

keyTerms.meaning: The second week
In the daytime, during the days
While being a זבה, with irregular bleeding

steps.confusionAlert: Night immersions and day immersions here come from different possibilities. Night is for a girl's fourteen days ending; day is for a זבה finishing her seven clean days.

phrases.english: The second week,
we make her immerse at night,
say: she gave birth to a girl.
[And] in the daytime,
phrases.notes: Some versions say בִּימָמָא, "by day"; the corrected wording is בִּימָמֵי, "during the days." The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: say: she gave birth to a boy while a זבה.
phrases.notes: A זבה immerses during the day when her seven clean days end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the week-by-week count of the 95 immersions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Week two needs nightly immersions in case of a girl, and daily immersions in case of a boy born while she was a זבה.

steps.title: Week three: immersing every day
steps.stepSummary: In the third week she immerses every day, in case she gave birth to a girl while she was a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the third week, we have her immerse in the daytime, because we can say: she gave birth to a girl while she was a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to week three of the count and explains the daytime immersions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who gives birth to a girl is impure for fourteen days, so if she had a girl, those days may have ended during week two. If she was a זבה, she then needs seven clean days, and those could end on any day of week three. Because a זבה immerses by day, she must immerse every morning of the third week.

keyTerms.meaning: The third week
A woman who gave birth to a girl while she was a זבה

phrases.english: In the third week, we have her immerse in the daytime,
phrases.notes: Some versions say בִּימָמָא, "by day"; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is בִּימָמֵי, "during the days," so every day.

phrases.english: because we can say: she gave birth to a girl while she was a זבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the week-by-week count after weeks one and two (steps 16-17).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In week three she immerses every day, in case she had a girl as a זבה and her seven clean days end that day.

steps.title: Week three: immersing every night, following בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: She also immerses every night of week three, because בית שמאי hold that a טבולת יום ארוך needs immersion.
steps.simpleTranslation: At night, she immerses too. This follows בית שמאי's own reasoning, since they say: a woman who is a 'טבולת יום ארוך' needs to immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the nighttime immersions of week three and explains that they come from the view of בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the impure days of childbirth comes a long stretch of 'pure days.' בית שמאי call a woman in that stretch a 'טבולת יום ארוך' and say she must immerse when it ends. Since we do not know when it ends for her, she immerses every night just in case.

keyTerms.meaning: Following their own reasoning, consistent with what they said elsewhere
A woman who immersed for a 'long day': she is in the long stretch of pure days after childbirth
Needs immersion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the nighttime immersions come from the זבה worry. The daytime ones are for the זבה case. The nighttime ones come only from בית שמאי's rule about a טבולת יום ארוך.

phrases.english: And at night, בית שמאי follow their own reasoning,
phrases.notes: The words 'she also immerses' are not written here, but the גמרא means them.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִי: טְבוּלַת יוֹם אָרוֹךְ בָּעֵי טְבִילָה.
phrases.english: since they say: a woman who is a 'טבולת יום ארוך' needs immersion.
phrases.notes: The 'long day' is the whole stretch of pure days after birth. This is from the משנה on 71b.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the nighttime immersions of week three, after step 18 covered the daytime ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, she also immerses every night of week three, because a טבולת יום ארוך needs immersion at the end of her pure days.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the number 95 in the ברייתא follows בית שמאי's view. Without their rule, the nighttime immersions would not be counted.
